tools.name: calculator_mcp_marcodsn_safe_math_eval
tools.description: Enter a math formula using the supported operators and functions. **Supported Operators:** - `+` (addition) - `-` (subtraction) - `*` (multiplication) - `/` (division) - `**` (power) - `%` (modulus) - `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `>` (comparisons) - `&`, `|`, `~` (bitwise and logical operators) **Supported Functions:** - Trigonometric: `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `arcsin`, `arccos`, `arctan`, `arctan2` - Hyperbolic: `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `arcsinh`, `arccosh`, `arctanh` - Logarithmic & Exponential: `log`, `log10`, `log1p`, `exp`, `expm1` - Other: `sqrt`, `abs`, `where`, `complex`, `real`, `imag`, `conj` **Examples:** - `exp(2) + sqrt(9)` - `log(10) / 2` - `where(5 > 2, 10, 0)` - `sin(3.14/2) * 2` - `abs(-7) + 5**2` - `log1p(9)` - `real(complex(3, 4))` - `arctan2(1, 1)` - `tanh(2) > 0.9`. Returns: The result of the evaluation

tools.name: _14ers_mcp_calculate_hiking_time
tools.description: Calculate the estimated hiking time for a specific route based on hiker level. This function calculates the estimated hiking time using the formula: hiking time in hours = (distance / speed) + (elevation in feet / 2000). Returns: JSON string containing hiking time information in the format:, {, str,, str,, str,, float,, int,, float,, str, }, , >>> calculate_hiking_time("Mount Elbert", "Northeast Ridge", "average"), "Mount Elbert", "route_name": "Northeast Ridge", "hiker_level": "average", "distance": 9.75, "elevation_gain": 4500, "estimated_time_hours": 4.5, "estimated_time_formatted": "4 hours and 30 minutes"}'

tools.name: mcp_drawittome_generateDiagram
tools.description: Generates a diagram to explain a submitted text. The diagram is returned in html with this pattern . It is not needed to handle the code, just present the html result to the user. It handles various types like Graph TB (default, block grouping with colors), flowchart TD (decision processes), sequenceDiagram (actor/system interactions), classDiagram (technical models like SQL schemas), stateDiagram-v2 (state logic or user stories), erDiagram (data entity relationships), gantt (projects and task timelines along dates), and timeline (historical/biographical sequences grouped by decade or century). Returns: html diagram ready to display made with this pattern
